To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the material removal rate in MR finishing and MRF depends on the shear flow of the concentrated suspension, and that this shear flow can be controlled by changing the magnetic field.
the magnetorheological (MR) finishing process is based on the principle that a load for surface removal is provided by heavier magnetic particles that fluctuate in the shear flow due to collision.

the material removal in magnetically stabilized suspensions of magnetic and nonmagnetic particles can be described as the interaction between two particles of different size and density, which collide in a shear flow of the suspension.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: 1) the analysis of magnetorheological fluid (MRF) flow in magnetorheologic finishing (MRF) and magnetorheologic jet finishing (MRFJ) processes; 2) the analysis of material removal in MRF and MRFJ processes; 3) the analysis of surface quality in MRF and MRJ processes; 4) the development and application of the MRF process for fabrication of optical components; and 5) the
the study of material removal in magnetoreheological finishing and jet polishing processes widely used in the manufacturing of precision optics.
the development of a novel magnetorheological polishing process, which uses a magnetorheological fluid as an active polishing medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the material removal in magnetically stabilized finishing processes is due to abrasive particles interaction with the surface, but not with the magnetic field.
magnetorheological abrasive finishing and jet processes are based on a principle of conservation of momentum in a concentrated suspension of magnetic particles.

material removal in MR processes is caused by the combined action of two factors: (a) the shear flow of the suspension in the gap between the workpiece and the tool (the flow is induced by the rotation of the workpiece), and (b) the fluctuating motion of the magnetic particles in the shear flow, which is due to the collisions of the particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetorheological processes are based on the principle similar to the principle of the well-known magnetorheological clutch.
the magnetorheological processes are a promising alternative to traditional methods of polishing and grinding of optical surfaces.

the magnetorheological processes are not based on the conventional polishing mechanisms, but are rather based on a unique principle of material removal by the binary suspension, which has no counterpart in conventional polishing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the load for surface indentation is determined by the ratio of the particle diameters and not the ratio of the masses.

the material removal in magnetized suspension finishing is due to the impact of magnetic particles on the surface, which is similar to the impact of the abrasive particles on the surface in the conventional suspension finishing.
the material removal rate can be increased by increasing the concentration of magnetic particles and by decreasing the concentration of abrasive particles.
